title: The First Olympics Had Just One Race
description: The ancient Olympic Games at Olympia, Greece.

scenes.narration: The first recorded Olympic Games had just one event: a running race.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Greek runners sprinting in a stadium at Olympia, crowds on grassy banks

scenes.narration: It's 776 BCE, at Olympia in Greece. Athletes race the length of the stadium, about 190 metres.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Olympia sanctuary with temples and a long earthen stadium

scenes.narration: Tradition says the winner is a cook named Koroibos.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Greek athlete crossing the finish line, raising arms, crowd cheering

scenes.narration: Over the centuries, wrestling, boxing and chariot racing are added.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Greek four-horse chariot race thundering around a hippodrome

scenes.narration: Athletes compete naked, and married women generally aren't allowed to watch.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Greek wrestlers in a sandy pit with judges holding rods, crowd

scenes.narration: Winners receive a crown of olive leaves, and become heroes back home.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Greek athlete being crowned with an olive wreath by a judge

scenes.narration: During the Games, a sacred truce lets athletes and fans travel safely.
scenes.image_prompt: crowds of ancient Greek travellers walking along a road toward Olympia

scenes.narration: The Games ran for over a thousand years. Which event would you enter?
scenes.image_prompt: ruins of the stadium entrance at Olympia today, green trees
